topic: Diagnosing parameter, polar-bound, and speed-versus-velocity errors

problems.desc: Part (b): a correct response says that dy/dx for a parametrised curve is the ratio (dy/dt) over (dx/dt), and the student stopped at dy/dt. Full credit states the chain-rule reason --- dy/dx = (dy/dt)(dt/dx) --- rather than only quoting the formula.

traps.desc: added the two components instead of taking the magnitude

problems.desc: Part (b): speed is the LENGTH of the velocity vector, so the components combine under a square root, not by addition. Full credit says the two components are perpendicular and combine the way the legs of a right triangle do; a response that only writes the formula without saying why addition is wrong earns half credit.

traps.desc: integrated from 0 to 2pi, which traces the circle twice

problems.desc: Part (b): a correct response says the curve r = 4 sin(theta) completes the whole circle as theta runs from 0 to pi, so integrating to 2pi sweeps every point a second time and doubles the area. Full credit includes how to detect this --- track where the radius returns to zero, or plot a few values of theta.

traps.desc: differentiated dy/dx with respect to t and stopped there

problems.desc: Part (b): the second derivative of a parametrised curve is the t-derivative of dy/dx divided AGAIN by dx/dt. The student produced the numerator only. Full credit states the divided form and notes that the units alone show the missing division.

traps.desc: integrated over 0 to 2pi, which sweeps every petal twice

problems.desc: Part (b): the bounds for ONE petal are the two consecutive values of theta at which the radius is zero, here minus pi over six and pi over six. Full credit solves 3 cos(3 theta) = 0 to find those bounds instead of guessing them, and says why a full turn cannot be the right interval for a single petal.

traps.desc: integrated the sum of the components instead of the magnitude

problems.desc: Part (b): arc length integrates the SPEED, which is the square root of the sum of the squared components; the student integrated each component separately and added the results, which measures neither distance nor displacement. Full credit says the square root cannot be split across a sum.

traps.desc: used dr/dtheta as the slope of the tangent line

problems.desc: Part (b): dr/dtheta measures how fast the radius changes, not the slope in the xy-plane. A correct response converts to x = r cos(theta) and y = r sin(theta) first, then takes (dy/dtheta) over (dx/dtheta). Full credit names both derivatives that the product rule contributes.

traps.desc: took the magnitude of the position vector instead of the velocity vector

problems.desc: Part (b): a correct response computes the acceleration vector, forms its dot product with the velocity vector, and reports the sign. Here the dot product is positive, so the speed is increasing at that instant. Full credit uses the dot-product test (or the derivative of the speed) rather than asserting from the picture; it must also say that the magnitude of the position vector plays no part in this.
